tasks.short: Review logistics service results with customers and agree improvements.

steps.what: Retrieve delivery events, shipment volumes and exception records.
Reconcile delivery events and calculate agreed service measures.
Prepare the customer review pack with trends, targets and service failures.
Assess causes, disputed results and proposed remedies before the review.
Discuss results with the customer and agree improvements within delegated authority.
Send the customer an action summary with owners and due dates.

tasks.design: A reusable import template or connector brings {OPS_SYSTEM} events into a governed calculation job on the {DATA_PLATFORM}, with results in {BI}. A template generator produces the review pack in {DOCS}; agreed actions entered through {WORKFLOW} produce a customer summary sent through {EMAIL} after approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Customer-specific metric definitions, disputed delivery timestamps and manual joins made reliable reporting costly to maintain.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting features, scheduled imports and deterministic checks cover most preparation. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building customer-specific mappings and templates.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing what counts as late, separating carrier failures from customer delays, and negotiating remedies.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the customer's operational consequences and make credible commitments when the figures are disputed.

ambition.what: Weekly service-recovery prioritisation for accounts previously reviewed monthly

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from rebuilding packs to investigating recurring failures and following through with customers. The logistician can prioritise recovery actions within existing authority; contract concessions still require the existing approver.

reach.task: Investigate recurring late-delivery patterns across customer accounts.
reach.learn: Metric definitions, cohort comparisons and the difference between correlation and an operational cause.

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-10 for access; 10-30 additional if national rules require employee consultation

evidence.claim: Service metrics, trend charts and standard review packs can use deterministic calculations and templates.
Customer discussions and disputed operational causes still require contextual judgement.

assumptions: Time shares describe a typical review cycle, not measured customer data.
Service targets have a validated structured matrix; interpreting new contract clauses is outside this build.
The scope starts with one event source and one review template; build ranges are estimates.
GDPR applies to personal data. Assess EU AI Act scope and national rules if the design changes to worker evaluation.
unknowns: Which delivery events and customer identifiers can be exported?
Who approves service definitions and benchmark sources?
Does the existing {BI} already provide the required measures and pack exports?
Do employee-level measures trigger consultation under applicable national rules?
research_questions: Can existing reporting configuration replace the proposed calculation job?
Which event checks best detect missing scans, duplicate deliveries and retrospective corrections?
new_work: Review data exceptions before customer use.
Maintain service definitions, source mappings and benchmark dates.
Monitor imports and investigate failed reconciliation checks.

tasks.short: Allocate available materials and products while resolving shortages and competing priorities.

steps.what: Check available stock, reservations, inbound receipts and quality holds.
Check order demand, required dates and commercial priorities.
Compare supply with demand and prepare allocations and shortage exceptions.
Resolve competing priorities with planning and sales, then approve allocations within delegated limits.
Enter approved reservations and allocation changes.
Notify dispatch and planning of allocation changes and unresolved shortages.

tasks.design: Configure allocation rules in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, using an integration from the {ERP} for demand and commercial priorities. A shortage view in {WORKFLOW} supports human decisions; approved allocations update the {OPS_SYSTEM} only after freshness and quantity checks, then trigger internal notices through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock, demand and commercial priorities sat in different records, while shortage decisions depended on informal context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reservation and allocation features can handle stable rules. Smaller integrations and exception forms are cheaper to build and maintain with AI-assisted coding.
tasks.still_hard: Uncertain inbound dates, inaccurate physical stock and choosing which customer bears a shortage.
tasks.human_edge: Balance service consequences, production dependencies and commitments when available stock cannot satisfy everyone.

ambition.what: Intraday shortage reallocation after confirmed supply changes

tasks.altitude: The logistician spends less time collecting positions and entering reservations, and more time resolving shortages. Within delegated limits, they can approve reallocations during the day instead of waiting for a consolidated planning round.

reach.task: Adjust the production sequence when a material shortage changes feasible output.
reach.learn: Bill-of-material dependencies, frozen planning windows and production changeover constraints.

build_days.consent_and_access: 4-12 for access; 10-40 additional if changed worker monitoring requires national consultation

evidence.claim: Stock reservations and allocations under explicit priority rules are standard deterministic operations capabilities.
Concurrent reservations require freshness checks and transactional controls to avoid allocating the same stock twice.

assumptions: Time shares are estimates for a mixed routine-and-shortage workload.
The {OPS_SYSTEM} supports configurable allocation rules and controlled reservation updates.
The {ERP} supplies demand separately from the {OPS_SYSTEM}; combined installations need less integration.
Approval covers an identified plan version; changed quantities or priorities invalidate that approval.
The design allocates goods rather than evaluating workers. GDPR, EU AI Act scope and applicable national rules still require assessment.
unknowns: How current and accurate are stock, quality holds and inbound confirmations?
Which priorities are contractual and which can the logistician change?
Can the {OPS_SYSTEM} reject stale or duplicate reservation updates?
Which integrations and permissions already exist?
Does rollout change employee monitoring or working arrangements?
research_questions: Can configured allocation rules represent expiry, batch, location and customer restrictions?
What is the safest supported method for atomic reservation updates?
new_work: Review shortage exceptions and explain overrides.
Maintain priority rules and effective dates.
Handle stale-plan rejections and failed updates.
Reconcile digital availability with physical stock discrepancies.

tasks.short: Redesign goods flows by comparing cost, service and operational feasibility.

steps.what: Extract shipment histories, routes, handling events and capacity use.
Retrieve transport, storage and handling costs for the same scope.
Reconcile costs and volumes into a baseline movement model.
Observe operations and validate handling, capacity and service constraints with site staff.
Develop alternative goods flows and compare cost, service and capacity under demand scenarios.
Select a feasible design and approve the trial scope and spending limits.
Document the chosen design, assumptions, trial measures and rollback conditions.

tasks.design: A reusable scenario tool imports {OPS_SYSTEM} movements and {ERP} costs into the {DATA_PLATFORM}, reconciles the baseline and runs constrained optimisation with explicit assumptions. It compares alternatives in {BI} and generates the approved design brief in {DOCS}; operational changes proceed through a separately approved trial in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Joining movement and cost data, encoding local constraints and rebuilding scenarios required specialist effort for each project.
tasks.enabler_now: Established optimisation methods already solve defined routing and flow problems. AI-assisted coding makes the surrounding imports, constraint forms and comparison views cheaper to assemble.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the right objective, capturing physical constraints, estimating uncertain demand and proving benefits during a live trial.
tasks.human_edge: Notice constraints absent from records and judge whether projected savings justify disruption and service risk.

ambition.what: Monthly goods-flow redesign screening using current demand and cost assumptions

tasks.altitude: The logistician spends more time testing operational hypotheses and observing trials. They gain scope to initiate scenario studies and recommend bounded trials; spending and network changes retain management approval.

reach.task: Test alternative goods flows during a depot closure or carrier outage.
reach.learn: Disruption scenarios, recovery priorities and minimum viable service levels.

reach.task: Turn the approved movement plan into a measured operational trial.
reach.learn: Dependencies, trial acceptance criteria and rollback planning.

build_days.consent_and_access: 5-15 for access; 10-40 additional if national consultation applies to changed working arrangements

evidence.claim: ORTEC documents route-planning use for Albert Heijn, supporting the feasibility of software-assisted movement planning.
Defined goods-flow scenarios can use optimisation and sensitivity analysis without a language-model loop.
A model's operational value depends on validated constraints and subsequent trial results.

assumptions: Time shares cover one bounded redesign study, including management approval.
The initial build covers one goods-flow scope, not a complete multi-country network.
Custom deterministic optimisation is needed only where existing planning configuration cannot express the scenarios.
Build estimates cover tool testing and a limited pilot; sustained benefit measurement may take longer.
GDPR applies to personal data; assess EU AI Act scope and national rules before including worker evaluation or changing working arrangements.
unknowns: What planning and optimisation features are already licensed and usable?
Which costs are avoidable rather than allocated accounting costs?
Which handling, safety, customer and capacity constraints are binding?
Who can approve trials, spending and changes to working arrangements?
How much historical data and trial capacity are available?
research_questions: Can existing planning configuration handle the required scenario scope?
Which optimisation formulation represents the important constraints at acceptable runtime?
How should trial results separate design benefits from demand and price changes?
new_work: Maintain constraint versions and cost assumptions.
Review infeasible scenarios and unrealistic recommendations.
Compare forecasts with actual trial performance.
Update models when routes, contracts or operating practices change.

tasks.short: Prepare and present logistics proposals that explain options, trade-offs and implementation requirements.

steps.what: Collect the approved solution, supporting analysis and relevant service commitments.
Clarify the audience's concerns, decision requested and constraints with the proposal sponsor.
Write the proposal and prepare presentation material for the intended audience.

loop.input: Approved source extracts, audience brief and a fixed proposal schema with permitted claims.
loop.output: Proposal sections and slide text with source references; missing facts become explicit questions.
loop.check: Validate required sections and source identifiers; insert figures from structured data and flag unsupported claims for the next review step.
loop.stop: One draft and at most one repair pass within a fixed token budget; unresolved sections fall back to the source-filled template.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle layout and figures, but explaining unfamiliar trade-offs in audience-specific prose requires bounded language generation.

steps.what: Check the proposal against source evidence and approve its claims and commitments.
Present the proposal, answer questions and discuss objections with stakeholders.
Send approved material and a checked summary of decisions and open questions.

tasks.design: A reusable proposal generator gathers approved sources from {DOCS}, fills figures and charts deterministically, and uses one bounded drafting loop for audience-specific explanations. The logistician checks claims before presentation; structured decision notes populate a follow-up through {EMAIL}, with approval at sending.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence collection and formatting could be automated, but adapting explanations to different audiences still required substantial writing.
tasks.enabler_now: Document templates and source-linked bounded drafting can combine reliable figures with editable prose. No autonomous negotiation or new reasoning breakthrough is required.
tasks.still_hard: Knowing what will persuade the audience, handling objections and recognising when a requested commitment exceeds authority.
tasks.human_edge: Read the room, explain uncertainty honestly and build agreement around operational trade-offs.

ambition.what: A two-option logistics decision brief for smaller operational improvement requests

tasks.altitude: Writing and formatting take less of the week, leaving more time for sponsor discussions and rehearsal. The logistician can prepare a wider range of decision briefs, while commercial and investment approval rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Frame a logistics proposal as a business case with explicit alternatives.
reach.learn: Benefits assumptions, sensitivity analysis and clear decision requests.

reach.task: Translate accepted proposal commitments into delivery milestones.
reach.learn: Scope boundaries, acceptance criteria and responsibility assignment.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-8 for source access; 10-30 additional if national consultation requirements apply

evidence.claim: Approved-source drafting can be bounded by templates, source references and a human approval step.
The digest documents a report with fabricated sources and a partial refund, supporting explicit source verification.

assumptions: Time shares describe a proposal with both written material and a live presentation.
The source pack contains approved analysis; the drafting loop does not create savings estimates.
The logistician approves claims within delegated authority and escalates new contractual or spending commitments.
Build ranges cover one proposal family and one document store.
GDPR applies where source material contains personal data. Assess EU AI Act scope and applicable national rules for the actual deployment.
unknowns: Which proposal templates and source documents are approved?
What information may be shared with each audience?
Who must approve pricing, contract changes and investment commitments?
Which processing arrangements are permitted for confidential source text?
Does an existing {DOCS} feature already provide sufficient source-linked drafting?
research_questions: How reliably can draft claims be traced to exact approved passages?
Which sections benefit from generated prose rather than fixed templates?
What review view makes changed figures and unsupported commitments easiest to detect?
new_work: Review generated claims, omissions and audience fit.
Maintain approved templates and source permissions.
Record unanswered questions and route commitment requests to the correct approver.
Check draft quality when sources or drafting instructions change.

role.altitude: The role moves from assembling positions and documents toward resolving shortages, testing goods-flow changes and leading customer decisions. Authority expands through explicitly delegated allocation and trial limits, rather than through unrestricted automated action.
reach: Logistics analysis: investigate recurring service failures using consistent measures.
Business continuity planning: test alternative goods flows under disruptions.
Project management: run bounded trials with acceptance and rollback criteria.
Management analysis: compare operational options through explicit business cases.
skills_to_grow: Service metric definitions and data reconciliation
Allocation policies and transactional stock controls
Customer negotiation and clear proposal writing
Source verification, access control and exception handling
role.ambitious_version: Run a small logistics improvement service that combines frequent shortage decisions, proactive customer recovery and measured goods-flow trials, using reusable tools that start from permitted exports.
